fields.label: Intro sentence
paragraphs: A moulded rubber pad with two legs at an angle, so it packs in one plane and locates in the other. The included angle is moulded to a stated tolerance, not left to shrinkage.

fields.label: Wrong default, a missing option, and one point specific to the shape
paragraphs: 🛑 Natural rubber is not offered, and it has the best fatigue resistance, highest resilience and least creep of the eight — which is what a pad holding a gap for years is judged on.
🛑 EPDM is pre-selected. It weathers well and creeps more under sustained load, and on a pad whose job is to hold a gap, creep is the failure.

🛑 And the angle changes one ranking. An internal corner concentrates stress, so tear strength matters more on this shape than on a flat pad — which moves silicone down and natural rubber, the best of the eight for tear, further up.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked.

fields.label: Selector
columns: Why, for an angled packing pad
rows: Best fatigue resistance, least creep and the best tear strength of the eight — and tear strength matters here, because an internal corner is where an angled section splits. Not for oil, and it perishes in prolonged sunlight
Where the pad is exposed to weather or sees oil. Good fatigue life and reasonable tear strength, with better ozone resistance than natural rubber
Low-cost enclosed packing. Fatigue and tear below natural rubber, and no oil resistance
Weather, ozone and steam. Creeps more than natural rubber, so allow for it in the deflection
Where the pad sits in oil. Poor ozone resistance, so not for an exposed corner
Lowest tear strength of the eight, and an internal corner is a tear origin. Specify only where temperature leaves no choice
Expensive sealing compounds with no fatigue, creep or tear advantage in a packing pad

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: It packs and locates at the same time
The flat leg holds the gap; the upstand stops the assembly creeping sideways and protects the corner. A flat pad does the first job only — which is the whole reason to choose this shape.
🛑 Rubber does not cure at the angle you cut

Shrinkage pulls the two legs against each other, so a cavity cut at 90° does not reliably give a part at 90°. We cut the tool with compensation and give the angle a stated tolerance — because a pad two degrees out bears on an edge, not a face.
The inside corner is where it fails
An internal angle concentrates stress, and a square root is where a flexing section splits first. We radius it in the tool, and we rank compounds on tear strength as well as on load.
One leg carries load and the other locates — they rarely need the same section. Tell us what each leg does and we will set them independently rather than moulding a uniform angle and hoping.
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change and no new element.
Card 02 is the strongest card on the page because it admits a manufacturing difficulty and then says how it is handled. A buyer who has received out-of-square angle sections before will recognise it immediately, and nobody else in this market puts it in writing.
Card 04 offers a design freedom rather than a feature, which is the more useful thing to give an engineer

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: The angle compensation belongs in the process
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · the same text as all 31 pages

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The compound is chosen for creep and tear resistance, since an angled section fails at its inside corner.
Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The cavity angle is cut with shrinkage compensation, and the inside corner is radiused rather than square.
Compression moulding, or extrusion and cutting where the section is supplied by the metre.
Post-cure and trimming, with adhesive backing applied where specified.
Quality inspection — included angle gauged against the drawing tolerance, plus leg dimensions, hardness and load-deflection on batch samples.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Angle sections are packed nested and unloaded, since rubber stored under compression takes a set and the angle can be forced. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept. The live text says “ISO-certified lab” in step 01, which becomes “in-house lab”; step 03 says “Compression Moulding” alone and gains the extruded route.
🛑 Step 02 is the engineering point of the sheet — shrinkage compensation on the cavity angle is the difference between a section that sits flat and one that rocks, and naming it as a tooling decision is what demonstrates Margo has made angled sections before.
Step 05 gauges the angle, which turns the tolerance from a claim into a check.
Step 06 carries a hazard specific to this shape: an angle stacked under load can be bent as well as compressed

notes: The process block must render from the part record, and on this page it has two possible routes.
“Shrinkage compensation” and “included angle gauged” are the credibility markers here.
Numbered steps are an <ol>.

fields.label: Credit, an addition, a caution
paragraphs: ISO 9001:2015 claimed and nothing else — no IATF, no TÜV SÜD, no CE marking. The production table prints “On request” rather than inventing figures, and the video says “Film pending”. The scope covers a moulded pad, so the badge stands unqualified.

🛑 Any rubber load pad invites the structural-bearing misreading. Elastomeric bridge and building bearings are certified products under EN 1337, with CE marking and third-party surveillance, and Margo holds none of it. An angled section used as corner packing on a structure is exactly the enquiry that would arrive.
